summary: Negative credit line and cents-level rounding discrepancy after clock-skewed usage postbacks from edge proxies
description:
Issue summary: Customer Ledgerly reported a small negative credit line (-$0.03) on their monthly invoice for 2026-02-28. The credit references an automatic adjustment labeled 'hourly_metering_reconciliation'. Impact: customer is concerned about unexplained negative credit lines and cents-level rounding affecting their automated accounting exports. Environment: dedicated account, us-west serving region, hourly metering enabled, reserved capacity with burst.

Observed behavior: an automatic reconciliation job created a negative credit (-$0.03) on a line item for time window 2026-02-28T05:00:00Z-06:00:00Z. The customer says they did not change usage and their internal meter shows no duplicate requests in that hour.

Steps to reproduce observed invoice line (investigation reproduction steps):
1) Review ingestion logs for hourly aggregator for 2026-02-28 05:00 UTC.
2) Inspect postback event ordering for Ledgerly's edge proxies (proxy host ids: ledgerly-edge-01..03).
3) Replay postbacks into metering staging pipeline with original timestamps and with corrected NTP-synced timestamps.

Expected behavior: reconciliation job should create either zero net adjustment or a positive charge if duplicates were found; rounding should not create a negative credit unless a true overcount occurred.

Actual behavior: reconciliation computed a -$0.03 credit. Preliminary evidence shows out-of-order postbacks with timestamps ~30s earlier than upstream ingestion due to clock skew. The aggregator's dedupe logic used (event_id + timestamp) to detect duplicates; when an out-of-order postback arrived with a timestamp less than the previously recorded one, the reconciliation path applied a differential tariff (reserved->hosted) before rounding, producing a small negative residual credit after the rounding step.

Attachments: excerpts from ingestion logs, reconciliation job output (below) and meter postback payload samples included in comments.
steps_to_reproduce: Pull ingestion logs for account Ledgerly around 2026-02-28T05:00:00Z - 2026-02-28T05:05:00Z
Identify postback event_ids and their timestamps from ledgerly-edge-01..03
Replay the same postbacks into the metering staging pipeline and compare reconciliation outputs with production
Toggle NTP-corrected timestamp on edge postbacks and observe adjustment behavior

comments: 2026-03-10 10:22 - Aisha Patel: Opened on behalf of Ledgerly finance (attached invoice screenshot). They see a -$0.03 line labeled 'hourly_metering_reconciliation' and want explanation before they post month-end entries.

2026-03-10 14:04 - Marcus Chen: Assigned. Initial triage: looks like a reconciliation rounding edge-case. Asking SRE to pull ingestion logs + edge proxy timestamps. Filing INT ticket for deeper ingestion trace (INT-4812).

2026-03-11 09:30 - SRE (J. Alvarez): Found NTP drift on ledgerly-edge-02 (~30s behind) for the window. Two postbacks for same event_id arrived with different timestamps; our dedupe key includes timestamp which caused the reconciler to compute a differential. Copying sample logs to this ticket.

2026-03-11 11:18 - Marcus Chen: Replayed events into staging reconciler with both original and corrected timestamps. With corrected (NTP-synced) timestamps, no adjustment generated. With original out-of-order timestamp, reconciler produced -$0.03 due to reserved->hosted tariff interpolation followed by rounding. Will propose a fix to dedupe logic.

2026-03-12 08:05 - Ledgerly (M. Ito): Thanks for quick triage — they request a formal explanation and a one-time credit to avoid manual reconciliation on their side if fix will take more than 48 hours.

2026-03-12 15:40 - Marcus Chen: CS proposed temporary manual credit of $0.03; awaiting billing approval. Engineering to implement dedupe change to prefer event_id-only deduping (with timestamp used only for window assignment) — tracked in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/412
investigation_notes: Root cause hypothesis: edge proxies with NTP drift emitted duplicate postbacks with identical event_id but different timestamps. Aggregator dedupe key used (event_id + timestamp) causing the reconciliation path to treat the out-of-order record as a separate usage and then apply a retroactive differential adjustment when it observed the true ordering.

Tariff interpolation path: when an out-of-order event shifts assignment between reserved and hosted rate buckets within the same hour, the reconciler computes a fractional adjustment. The rounding function applied at final line-item level can produce small negative values in a tiny percentage of cases when the adjustment magnitude is near 0 and sign flips due to floating point/cent rounding.
Staging repro confirmed: replay with original timestamps reproduces -$0.03. Replaying with normalized NTP-corrected timestamps yields no adjustment.
proposed_fix: Engineering proposes changing dedupe to key on event_id only and to perform window-assignment using the ingestion_arrival_time (server-side canonical time) rather than client-provided timestamp for dedupe decisions. Also add a final reconciliation floor to prevent sub-cent negative credits (treat adjustments < $0.01 as zero) and log hits for auditing.
resolution: Pending billing approval for one-time manual credit of $0.03. Engineering PR merged to staging (https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/412) implementing event_id-only dedupe and final-floor logic. Rollout plan: canary to prod-us-west on 2026-03-15, full rollout 2026-03-17. Once change is in prod, we will reverse the manual credit if not required.
